steps.text: Measure out all ingredients before starting. Grease a large rimmed baking sheet; set aside.
Combine sugar, corn syrup, water, and salt in a heavy, 2-quart saucepan over medium heat.
Stir until sugar is completely dissolved and the mixture comes to a boil, about 5 minutes.

Stir in peanuts and set a candy thermometer in place. Continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until the temperature reaches 300 to 310 degrees F (150 to 155 degrees C). Don’t be tempted to stir too much as this can make the brittle turn grainy.

Remove from the heat. Quickly stir in butter and baking soda, then immediately pour mixture onto the prepared baking sheet. Quickly use 2 forks to lift and pull the mixture into a 12x14-inch rectangle. Let cool until completely firm, at least 30 minutes.
Use a mallet to break peanut brittle into pieces.

raw_recipe.headline: Mom’s Best Peanut Brittle
raw_recipe.description: This homemade peanut brittle is easy to make with this foolproof recipe for a sweet, salty, crunchy treat that wows everyone, every time! Great for gifts.

review.reviewBody:
Wow! For those of you who put in 2 cups of peanuts, you must really like a lot of nuts! 
I put in about 1 & 1/4 cups and stopped there. 
I didn't even attempt the fork idea. I kept my cookie sheet warm in the oven while the candy was cooking. When I poured the mixture onto the warm pan, it stayed soft long enough for me to then tilt the pan to spread the candy out.

Great Brittle. A few tips: Be sure to have butter and baking soda measured out beforehand and waiting, (and butter softened) stir them in well to mix, but dont stir it to death. when it is foamy and pale, stir a few times more, and then stop. I doubled the recipe (a single recipie for a single household, double it to share with anyone) and used a half-sheet size (read: about 17"x13" with a lip on it about an inch tall. I covered the pan with extra-wide aluminum foil and buttered the foil, and the sides of the foil. As soon as you are done stirring the stuff in, pour it onto the foil, and spread it out. I did this by picking the pan up and kind a shaking it around. If you try to spread it around like frosting, you'll end up breaking all those beautiful little bubbles that make it crunchy but light. Have fun!

This is the recipe my family has used for 30 years and always gets rave reviews. Certainly a candy thermometer would be helpful but we've never used one. I was taught to cook the syrup until the stir spoon held about two feet above the pot has a long thin thread going down to the pot - then stir in the peanuts and cook until the peanuts are tan. Mix in the rest in one quick motion and spread on WARM cookie sheets to help it spread. 
Yummm.

Perfect! Definitely use a candy thermometer and add peanuts around 280 degrees so they don't burn. (The color was still a pretty golden tan.) I added 1tsp vanilla at the end, used lightly salted peanuts, and left out the salt. I also placed parchment paper on my granite counter and then poured the mixture right on top with much success. Sets up very quickly! My 4 kids loved it! I'll be making this for years to come! Don't pass up this recipe! UPDATE: I made about 10 yummy batches for Christmas gifts. I learned to completely stir in all the butter at the end or the brittle won't have a pretty sheen. Also, DO NOT DOUBLE the recipe. The result is burnt peanuts. You can wait until 300 degrees to add the peanuts too. I found this made it easier to stir the mixture up until this point. My average for the recipe to reach 300 degrees was about 10-11 min.

My husband and I made this last night and we both agreed this was the BEST peanut brittle. So crispy and buttery---YUM!
PS: I did add a teaspoon of Vanilla to this recipe. It's just something my mom always did. 
5 stars!

I added 1 tablespoon of minced Jalapeños, everybody went wild! It's my most requested candy, made 5 batches for a family event and they were hiding the candy from each other. I added the peppers during the cooking process before taking off stove and adding the peanuts, the heat intensifies as it sits.

I have made this several time, usually a double batch. The only thing I do different is add a little vanilla and almond extracts and use an extra 1/2 cups of peanuts. I also take it to 320-340*. It's very buttery and so good.

I personally add 1 tsp of vanilla to every batch for a nice secondary note of flavor to go with that rich butteriness! To all you 4 stars and below, be sure to use a candy thermometer, gradually turn up your heat on your gas and induction stoves, Also, use a wooden flat spoon so that when you’re constantly stirring you can scrap the bottom of your pot. If you have and older electric stove it may be that it cannot hold the temp at a constant temperature; I’ve noticed this on older ranges. The pic is of a DBL batch with 20% (1/2 tsp) more baking soda to ensure brittleness. This was spread out on a 13”x10” pan. I like my PB think and brittle. There was even a little extra for the confectioner! For deeper flavors leave it on the stove or hot plate until it get darker or 310°F. I took mine off at 305°F. Turned out perfect! =)

Taste is great and it breaks easily when cooled. I added a tablespoon of vanilla and 1/4 cup of very finely chopped pecans - nice additional flavor. 

Do not turn the heat completely off when adding ingredients, the sugar starts to cool too fast when adding the cold ingredients. Also use a metal stirring spoon, plastic spoons bend too easy. Pour fast onto a heated pan lined with parchment paper to make spreading it easier.

"Just made this for first time. Cooked to temperature as directed.. 300o F. Candy is bendable not hard. Sticking to my teeth. Disappointed." Hard crack is 302. I go to 305 to be sure entire mix is at temp. Beyond that tends to burn.

I researched all of the reviews before I made this. I doubled the recipe because I had a big pan to fill. I ended up using dark corn syrup because that's all I had- it gave it a nice colour. I had everything measured and they aren't kidding when they say be ready. I did take the advice of heating up the pan and kind of shaking it side to side to even out the brittle- it worked like a charm. It did take longer than I expected for the thermometer to heat up to 300. I actually thought they thermometer was broken so I turned up the heat. I then didn't stir enough and burned a couple of peanuts. My best tip would be to be patient! But as soon as it hits 250, it's quick from there. I am pleased to share that my first ever batch of peanut brittle was a complete success! Great recipe!

I followed the recipe to the letter and it all worked out fantastic and delicious! My only issue was not knowing how long to expect it to take to get to 150C. I made a single batch in a 3.6L (~15 cup) saucepan and the mixture was only about a 1/2” thick on the bottom which meant my candy thermometer wasn’t getting deep enough. I had to keep tilting the pot and putting the thermometer in the thicker pool of liquid to get a proper reading. On an induction stove, this meant that every time I tilted the pot off the surface, it would stop the heat so there was inconsistency. This resulted in it taking almost an hour to reach the proper temperature. Don’t know how that compares with how long it “should” take, but it ended up turning out well in the end. It’s light & crisp, and not sticky on the teeth - just the way I’d hoped it would be, and that’s why you should never skip the Baking Soda. I’d make this again, but in a smaller pot to obtain a deeper solution for the thermometer.
Easy to make and tastes amazing!
310 degrees extra peanuts worked

Like a few others I decided to use roasted peanuts instead of raw peanuts only because they are more available to me. My one piece of advice is if you decide to use already roasted nuts do not put them in until you are much closer to the three-hundred-degree mark. This will keep the nuts from getting scorched.
I love this recipe and I am really upset that it’s so easy, I love peanut brittle and it loves my hips!
Very simple to follow
Easy recipe to follow. 10 /10!!!! It turned out perfect. GREAT recipe and this was my first time ever making peanut brittle. Will definitely make on repeat. It tastes amazing. Thank you so much.

This recipe is perfect! I did preheat my pan to help spread the mixture in the pan once the brittle was ready to poor. I pulled the brittle from the heat as soon as the thermometer hit 300 degrees and immediately added the butter and baking soda and mixed thoroughly until butter was incorporated. I doubled the batch, added an extra cup of nuts, and it filled a regular half sheet almost perfectly. Light and crispy. Just like my grandma used to make.
Perfect Brittle , I added vanilla last . This was the first decent easy easiest recipe and delish!! 🎄🎄
